adjudication.rationale: In EventManager, the BookingReference construction was changed to use `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and to drop the previous fallback to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (e.g. `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined`, and similarly later `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`). In this diff, only `CalendarManager.createEvent` was extended to return `externalId`/`credentialId` (it now accepts `externalId?: string` and returns `{ externalId, credentialId: credential.id }`), but there is no corresponding change shown for `CalendarManager.updateEvent` to populate `result.externalId` (or guarantee `result.credentialId`). If update flows (reschedule/update) reuse this BookingReference-building logic, calendar references will lose `externalCalendarId` (and potentially `credentialId`), degrading future updates/cancels. The mismatch between the new consumer (`result.externalId`) and the unchanged update producer is directly evidenced by the diff.
